title: Fixed Beaded Loop Drum and Turned Grip Cabasa
description: One newly authored complete fixed-display cabasa-style beaded-loop percussion prop: a single turned grip with a broad flat butt enters the whole wide short cylinder core, with two full rounded wooden end discs retaining five entire closed beaded loops around the cylinder. Each loop is a continuous closed swept surface whose radius alternates from short thin links into rounded faceted beads; it is not a row of loose unconnected balls or a painted stripe. The original opaque core is visible between the loops. All geometry is new, no earlier yo-yo flange, cord, ratchet wheel or reed is extracted or transformed. The complete grip-core-end-disc-and-external-beaded-loop organization differs from the narrow axle and wound single string of the old yo-yo and the open frame, toothed wheel and anchored reed of the old noisemaker. Nine closed editable meshes with four opaque constant PBR appearances, one model and zero scenes. Metres, native Z up, horizontal bounds-centred ground origin on the finite flat grip butt. This is a fixed static illustrative pose: beads have small hidden core overlaps as display attachments, not a freely moving chain mechanism. No sound, friction, rotation, bead articulation, physical balance, manufacturing, child suitability, use or safety performance is claimed; no rig, animation or interaction is made.
